name: Kapsel
prior: PhISEM / STK Shakers (Cook): random collisions of many objects, 'a single noise source, one exponential decay and one second-order filter' for a maraca; types incl. rainstick-like tambourine/sleighbells/water drops, Csound STKShakers (V: ccrma.stanford.edu/~juanig/articles/wadi-icmc/Model_Maracas.html; csound.com/docs/manual/STKShakers.html; caml.music.mcgill.ca/~gary/307/week11/node12.html). Piepenbrink, 'Embedded Digital Shakers' (NIME 2018): handheld battery-powered PhISEM shakers with hand mutes and feedback (VS: nime.org/proc/piepenbrink2018). Mike Wilson (CCRMA 2010): accelerometer frame driving STK Shakers, rotation sets object count and resonance (VS: ccrma.stanford.edu/~mwilson/blog/2010-11-05.html). Grainstick (IRCAM, 2010): tilt makes grains move, 'if the tilt is very steep, a dense avalanche of grains happens' - the avalanche statistic exists as a tracked-controller installation (VS: quod.lib.umich.edu bbp2372.2010.024). IRCAM CoSC 'Rainstick' web app (2014): Web Audio, phone held horizontally and tilted, sample-based material by Jodlowski (VS: cosima.ircam.fr/2014/07/15/cosc-web-applications/). 'Rainstick' iOS app (P. Millerd): flips make rain noise (VS: apps.apple.com/us/app/rainstick/id6752230474). Rainbow Circuit Whistle (M4L): granular exciter into a banded-waveguide resonator (VS: synthanatomy.com 2023/12 whistle); Mutable Elements 'bouncy particles' exciter (V: research/synthesis.md 2.9). Myzel: Tropfen (per-drop automation pattern, APP 4512+), Hauch, Körner. Not found: a note-grid instrument whose tilt is the pour angle with Poisson seeds, avalanche clumps, after-run and a tuned tube that is excited into pitch by density.
costNotes: Native: noise source 0.06 + 4 biquads 0.24 + 3-4 gains 0.1 ~ 0.4; plus the DelayNode comb tube for f <= 375 Hz (+0.06-0.08, allowed in a cycle since DelayNode is in it, 128-frame minimum, R: webaudio.md section 7) -> 0.45 at L1. Automation: 2 events per seed, 80/s at the 40/s default, 160/s at dichte 80 (M: sim) per voice; Tropfen already schedules per-drop setValueAtTime/setTargetAtTime pairs from tick() (APP trp tick(), 25 ms clock, horizon 0.12-0.35 s), so the pattern is proven in the app; the a-rate timeline costs about a biquad while events are inside the block (R: section 4, ramping params ~ constant cost). 10 voices x 160 events/s = 1600 main-thread calls/s - cheap, but measure on Android as the idea itself asks. The 'tick' main-thread jitter (A.jitter) means seeds are scheduled 120-350 ms ahead: the Höhe response lag of 0.4 s in the idea must include this. L3 two tubes L/R + 5f + rate x 1.75 ~0.9.
soundHeld: The core promise 'ab einer Dichte singt das Rohr' is not in the DSP: bandpass + bandpass + lowpass is linear, so the tube rings identically for one seed or eighty - density only changes how continuous the ringing is. Worse, with Q 35 each seed is not a dry tick but a pitched ping: ring time tau = Q/(pi f) = 51 ms at 220 Hz, 203 ms at 55 Hz (M), so sparse seeds through the tube sound like Tropfen (tuned drops), and above ~20 seeds/s the pings overlap (mean overlap 1.0 at 20/s, 4 at 80/s, M) into a pitched noise band = Hauch. The rainstick identity (dry ticking) lives only in the dry/holz path. Fix: two paths - dry seeds (highpass bright / lowpass dark, holz) always, and the tube resonance mixed in by a smoothstep of the measured rate lambda (that is the missing nonlinearity, cheap: one gain set from tick()), with Q 35 and the 128-frame comb (closed tube: odd harmonics for free with negative feedback) only when the tube 'sings'. Then low y = dry trickle with a faint pitch, high y = roar with a note, and the avalanche L(t) modulates both. Bass columns: Q 35 at 55 Hz rings 0.9 s to -40 dB, the tube is a sine drone; lower Q with f (Q = 35 * sqrt(f/220)) keeps the body. The 0.4 s rate lag plus 1-2 s after-run under tilt is the right feel and is distinct from every other engine; Bebung on bp.detune does nothing audible on noise unless the tube is singing (fine).
soundBurst: As a Puls hit it is a pitched shaker/cabasa and that is good and rare in the library: 60-150 ms of dichte 1 with decay gives a 'tschk' whose tone is the lane note. Failure: at 60 ms the Poisson process at 40/s yields on average 2.4 seeds - a burst is 1-4 random ticks, not a shaker stroke; use a deterministic dense burst (seeds every 2-4 ms with random amplitude, i.e. 15-40 per hit) so every hit has the same weight, and the tube mix at full for the hit. Rassel candidate under Gestik (ladRassel) fits because a shake is exactly a dense burst.
failureModes: 'Tube sings only above a density' is not in the linear DSP; add an explicit density-driven tube mix (smoothstep of lambda) and keep a dry path
Q 35 bandpass turns each seed into a 50-200 ms pitched ping (M): sparse = Tropfen, dense = Hauch; identity needs the dry seeds and Q scaled with f
Puls burst of 60 ms at 40/s is 1-4 random seeds; use a deterministic dense burst per hit
Scheduling lag: seeds are planned 120-350 ms ahead (tick horizon), so Höhe/tilt response lags beyond the 0.4 s model lag; subtract horizon from the model
Automation load 160 events/s per voice at max density, 10 voices = 1600/s: proven pattern (Tropfen) but measure on mid-range Android
At f <= 375 Hz the comb tube has 128-frame-quantised pitch (R: section 7); use it only as a body behind the biquads, never as the tuning element
Gated noise is 'gate' not 'seed' unless lengths (0.5-3 ms), two tonings and clump statistics vary per event; the sim confirms 3 ms windows never overlap below 80/s, so the texture stays granular
verdict: Rare: PhISEM shakers with accelerometer control (CCRMA, NIME 2018), IRCAM's Grainstick avalanche and a Web Audio tilt rainstick (CoSC 2014) all exist, but none is a note-grid instrument with Poisson seeds, clumps, after-run and a tube that is pitched into song by density. Native at ~0.45 units with the app's proven per-event automation pattern (Tropfen), 80-160 events/s per voice to be measured on Android. The sketch's central nonlinearity - the tube sings only above a density - does not exist in a chain of biquads, and a Q-35 bandpass turns every seed into a 50-200 ms tuned ping, so sparse play sounds like Tropfen and dense play like Hauch (M). With a dry seed path, a density-driven tube mix, Q scaled with frequency and a deterministic dense burst per Puls hit it becomes the only engine in Myzel you pour with the wrist and the only pitched shaker on a lane; without those it is noise through filters.
